text:
The dust motes dance in light that starts to fade,
No whispered page-turns break the heavy air;
The catalog drawers stand with locks displayed,
And silence settles on the empty stair.
We packed the shelves into cardboard boxes tight,
Each spine a memory, each cover worn;
The fluorescent hum gives up its final bite,
Before the key turns in the iron door.
What once held worlds within these quiet rows
Now holds only shadows, deep and thin;
The story ends before the reader knows
How much of self was lost beneath the din.
The sign goes dark. The building breathes no more.
